title: Decision Lab
subtitle: Ask a decision model typed questions about a situation, and see the probability behind every answer.
explainer: A decision model does not write text. Given a state and a set of questions, it returns a choice with a probability for every candidate, the probability that a condition holds, or a score along an ordered scale. Those probabilities are the model's own output distribution, not a parse of prose. Ollama serves them on /v1/systemone; models that report only the decision capability belong here and nowhere else.
noModelsHint: Pull nimble, tev1, clef or clef-flash from the Models page; they report the decision capability and appear here.
statePlaceholder: Describe the situation every question is about: a ticket, a message, a log line, a document.

criteriaHint.choice: One per line, as name: description. 2 to 26 candidates.
criteriaHint.score: One per line, lowest first. The order is the scale. 2 to 26 steps.

problems.duplicateKey: Another question already uses this key.

results.title: Answers
results.footnote: Probabilities are what the model returned, unrounded except for display. The chosen candidate is the most probable one; a score is the expected position on your scale, so it can fall between two steps.
